messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: p99 latency breach for /v1/streaming/generate in us-west-2 canary cluster. Model=open-llm-v3.4-canary. p99=2.4s (SLO=1.2s). Traffic spike + increase in streaming stalls. Creating channel and paging oncall.
Alex Chen: I'm oncall, looking now. Any manual deploys or config flips in the last 30m?
Priya Rao: I'm seeing the same in dashboards — p95 up to 600ms, p99 ~2.4s. Streaming stall rate up x12 for canary subset. Errors are timeouts with large tail latency; backend health checks are OK.
Marco G: We pushed v3.4-canary at 09:12 UTC, gradual 5 -> 20% over 15m with traffic ramp rule traffic-shift-2026-03. No infra changes. KV cache hit-rate for encoder nodes dropped ~40% coincident with ramp.
Alex Chen: Noted. Is this region-specific?
Priya Rao: Mostly us-west-2; small signals in eu-west-1 but within noise. The stall traces point to encoder deserialization pauses and stalled socket writes on streaming connections.
Emily Stone: Heads up — Support got 3 escalations from enterprise customers in us-west-2 complaining about slow responses/timeouts; ticket ids: #CS-8721, #CS-8722, #CS-8723. They reported spikes starting ~09:25.
Jess K: Paging SRE lead for rollout rollbacks, looping in deploy-bot for quick traffic cut. @deploy-bot can we pause canary traffic?
deploy-bot: Command received: pause-traffic --policy traffic-shift-2026-03 --confirm. Executing...
Alex Chen: Hold on — before pausing, can we confirm fallbacks? If we cut canary immediately will traffic go to stable-default model?
Marco G: Yes, the routing policy has fallback to open-llm-v3.3-stable. Cut will route all canary traffic back to stable within ~15s per edge.
Priya Rao: I'd prefer immediate cut. p99 is double SLO and stall rate rising. We risk customer timeouts.
Alex Chen: OK pausing canary now. Marco, own exec and watch rollout metrics. Priya, own streaming traces and logs. Emily, coordinate customer comms. Jess, stay on call in case we need infra scaling.
Marco G: pausing...
deploy-bot: Traffic policy traffic-shift-2026-03 paused successfully. Canaries now at 0% in us-west-2, rollback target open-llm-v3.3-stable. Verified edge routing converging.
Alex Chen: Watching dashboards... p99 dropped to 1.1s within 90s. p95 back to 320ms. Looks like immediate mitigation working.
Priya Rao: Confirming stream stall rate down ~80%. KV cache hit-rate recovering. No new timeouts in last 2mins.
Emily Stone: Notifying affected customers: short note sent to #enterprise-notifications and CS queue — "We've routed traffic back to the stable model and are investigating. Expect normal response times. We'll follow up with a postmortem." Customers acknowledged.
Marco G: Creating rollback PR to pin stable model while we debug: internal link: https://repo.redwood/rollouts/pull/4821. Will also run a canary replay locally to reproduce.
Alex Chen: Good. Let's collect traces from a few of the stalled requests and get a heap/profile from an encoder pod in us-west-2. Priya, what's the retention window for streaming traces?
Priya Rao: We keep 1h in hot storage. I've exported the top 50 traces and uploaded to /tmp/incident-6789012345/traces.zip and shared with the oncall team.
Jess K: Ops: scaling policy for encoder-worker in us-west-2 increased from min=6 to min=8 as a precaution. Monitoring CPU and network.
Marco G: Noted. Initial hypothesis: v3.4 changed encoder serialization which increases cold-start deserialization cost; with traffic ramping it caused KV cache thrash and longer tails on socket writes. Need to run microbench on serialization path.
Alex Chen: Action items: (1) rollback/pause done (Marco) (2) collect traces and heap (Priya) (3) customer comms update (Emily) (4) run serialization microbench + reproduce (Marco) (5) follow-up postmortem (Alex). Assigning owners.
Priya Rao: I've attached the traces and a few logs: ``
[stream_session] id=abcd1234, duration=4.6s, stall_ms=1800, encoder_deserialize_ms=950
[encoder] gc_pause_ms=12, alloc_rate_mb=45, socket_write_wait_ms=1100
``
Marco G: Running local replay now, reproducing deserial cost spike when cache miss pattern matches production. I can reproduce ~1s extra latency on encoder deserialize.
Emily Stone: CS expects an incident summary for customers in 2 hours. I'll draft. Include action taken and ETA for postmortem.
Alex Chen: Once Marco confirms root cause reproducible, we can either revert v3.4 changes or ship a quick fix to serialization path. Keep coordination tight.
Priya Rao: All metrics stable for 5m. No regressions seen. I'll keep a watch on streaming stalls and set an alert for any rebound.
Marco G: Repro done. Filing a bug now: internal bug #BUG-9301. Will propose one of: revert serialization delta, adjust cache warmup, or add a brief rollout ramp hold.
Alex Chen: Thanks everyone. We'll keep this channel for status. If anything changes escalate immediately.
incident-bot: NOTE: Incident acknowledged and mitigation in progress. Severity set to Sev2. Paging suspended.
Alex Chen: Closing loop — p99 steady at 1.05s for last 6m, no active customer timeouts. I'll open a postmortem doc and assign follow-ups.
Emily Stone: Postmortem + customer note drafts saved: https://drive.redwood/incident-6789012345. Sending final customer update now.
Jess K: Moving to handoff to follow-up owners. Oncall shift ends in 25m, tagging next oncall. :thumbsup:
Alex Chen: Thanks all — great response. We'll reconvene in the postmortem. :raised_hands:
